PullRequest.Title: [Perf] agentHost: isolate E2E storage on tmpfs
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Isolate **Agent Host E2E tests only** from physical-storage latency while retaining required disk-backed lifecycle coverage.

- On Linux CI, run Agent Host replay on an executable, private 4 GiB tmpfs, then require a disk-backed persistence/lifecycle pass.
- Keep real SQLite files, transactions, migrations, connection close/reopen, idle eviction, deletion, and host-process restart. Local and non-Linux defaults remain disk-backed.
- Extend the required disk-backed selection to Agent Host detached-worktree archive/unarchive preservation, restoration after a host restart, and deletion recovery for a missing checkout.
- Keep the runner, coverage tooling, Windows launcher, and Linux mount wrapper together under `test/integration/agentHost`; update package commands, integration entrypoints, and CI change detection.
- Fail explicitly on mount, filesystem-probe, test, and unmount errors; use unique temporary roots outside instruction-bearing checkout directories.

No Git extension changes, production-code changes, or flaky-pipeline YAML changes are included. No deadlines, replay fixtures, assertions, SQLite durability settings, or product lifecycle ordering are changed. Tmpfs is not machine-crash durability coverage; the disk-backed pass remains required.

## Evidence

Related Linux lifecycle failures: [480990](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480990) and [481414](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481414).

Temporary diagnostic builds showed multi-second storage operations coinciding with substantial I/O pressure. [481449](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481449) alternated four disk and four tmpfs runs of an unchanged Agent Host workload on the same Linux worker; all eight passed:

| Measurement | Disk | Tmpfs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Workload duration | 71–77 s | 35–36 s |
| Median session restore | 586 ms | 119 ms |
| Metadata queue p95, including execution | 312 ms | 35 ms |
| Longest metadata queue | 3.72 s | 121 ms |
| Longest metadata read | 1.48 s | 62 ms |

The investigation's production timing instrumentation and experimental pipeline controls are not part of this PR. These measurements demonstrate a material storage-latency contribution, not proof that every original timeout is resolved.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed after merging current `main`.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStorage.integrationTest.ts` — 7 passed after the merge (six wrapper cases plus registry-cleanliness validation).
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --storage disk --jobs 6 --grep 'session metadata history and provider context survive a host restart|archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart|a created automation survives an agent host restart|automation lifecycle: cancelled request deduplication survives a restart|automation lifecycle: an unavailable model produces a durable failed run|regression coverage: cold resume retains ordered user and assistant context|regression coverage: identical prompts remain separate completed turns after resume|detached worktree safety:'` — 18 passed before the upstream merge, including the additional Agent Host worktree coverage.
- `npm run eslint -- test/integration/agentHost/runner.ts test/integration/agentHost/coverage.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStorage.integrationTest.ts .github/actions/detect-agent-host-e2e-changes/detect.ts` — passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts test/integration/agentHost/runner.ts test/integration/agentHost/coverage.ts test/integration/agentHost/tmpfs.sh test/integration/agentHost/child.ps1 src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStorage.integrationTest.ts` — passed.
- `bash -n test/integration/agentHost/tmpfs.sh` — passed.
- `node --test build/lib/testAgentHostE2EStartup.test.ts build/lib/electronVersion.test.ts` — 7 passed. The upstream Agent Host startup fixture now uses the relocated runner/Windows launcher and explicitly selects disk mode; this fixes the old-path `ENOENT` reported by Compile & Hygiene.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed before the upstream merge; the post-merge local check is blocked by the installed older `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` lacking the `/v1` declarations required by current `main`. Fresh CI installs from the merged lockfile.

Earlier packaged validations:

- [481451](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481451) — full Linux integration passed: 947 Agent Host tests on tmpfs, all 15 then-selected disk-backed lifecycle tests, and remaining integration suites.
- [481450](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481450) — two full Linux split-storage iterations passed.
- [481481](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481481) and [481482](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481482) — repeated Linux/Windows/macOS builds passed at the preceding revision.

[481510](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481510) and [481511](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=481511) both **passed** at the current revision, with successful Electron integration tasks on Linux, Windows, and macOS in each run. They validate the narrowed scope, expanded Agent Host disk selection, upstream merge, and corrected startup fixture.

In each accepted Linux build, all six Agent Host entrypoints passed on tmpfs (947 reported tests, approximately 254 seconds), followed by all 18 required disk-backed lifecycle tests (31–36 seconds). The three detached-worktree cases passed on both backings.

The [GitHub Code OSS workflow](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37571816304) passed at the current revision, including Compile & Hygiene and Linux/macOS/Windows Electron integration. Its isolated Linux unit-check rerun passed without code changes.

## How to test

On Linux with noninteractive mount privileges:

```sh
npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --storage split
```

Use `--storage disk` or `--storage tmpfs` for an explicit control, and `--grep` to select Agent Host scenarios. Split mode always runs the required disk-backed lifecycle selection, independent of the broad-pass filter.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux CI Agent Host E2E split-storage run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One outer runner performs runtime preparation, then synchronously waits for the full tmpfs replay pass, unmounts it, and synchronously waits for the required disk-backed lifecycle pass; both passes must finish before the integration job advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mount and unmount one private tmpfs through noninteractive sudo
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mount and one unmount per full split run, independent of test count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single E2E pass used the existing disk temporary directory and performed no mount subprocesses
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mount precedes all replay tests and unmount follows them, so both are on the critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch six suite-specific integration test processes, which transitively fork Agent Host and provider processes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to six suite processes concurrently in the broad pass; the disk pass launches the same six suite entrypoints with a grep selecting the required lifecycle cases
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same six suite entrypoints ran once against disk; the diff moves the broad pass to tmpfs and adds a narrowed second disk pass
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The slowest suite determines each pass duration; the two passes are serialized

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SQLite, fixture, checkout, archive, and temporary-user-data operations performed by the E2E tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Broad replay suite on one shared tmpfs mount, then a grep-selected lifecycle subset on disk; server leases coalesce process startup across up to 25 model-backed or 40 total tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All broad-suite storage operations used the normal disk-backed temporary directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Storage operations are on test critical paths; tmpfs removes physical-device latency from the broad pass while retaining disk coverage for the selected subset

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read seven bounded /proc snapshots and append one JSONL diagnostic record
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At start, every five seconds, and at pass completion for each Linux inner runner
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous sampling briefly runs in the runner process while child suites execute, but bounded proc records and one append do not establish material critical-path contention

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The broad suite's test count controls tmpfs filesystem work; the required disk grep has a fixed curated selection spanning six entrypoints, while runner concurrency is capped at six workers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within a pass, up to min(configured jobs, 6) suites run concurrently. The tmpfs and disk passes are strictly serialized; one tmpfs mount serves all broad-pass workers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each pass uses fresh test processes and isolated temporary state. Runtime preparation is initiated by the outer runner; child runners inherit VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH, while provider-server reuse remains bounded within each suite. OS caches may be warm for the second pass, but no new application cache determines fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: runner orchestration, environment propagation, mount lifecycle, suite cap, and transitive host forks are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact duration and tmpfs resident-memory use depend on worker load and suite data volume, but mount count, suite-process cardinality, pass ordering, and storage placement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra fixed disk subset is an explicit durability-coverage tradeoff, while the broad storage workload is moved off physical storage; diagnostics and mount overhead are bounded and small relative to the suite.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local and non-Linux Agent Host E2E execution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runner prepares Electron if needed and runs the six selected suite entrypoints against normal disk temporary storage; no split pass or mount occurs by default.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run npm install or Electron preparation only when runtime artifacts are absent or stale
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on a warm checkout; at most one preparation invocation per runner start when required
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The relocated runner used the same preparation checks and subprocesses
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold preparation blocks tests, as before

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run suite-specific integration scripts and transitive Agent Host/provider processes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six suite entrypoints with up to six concurrent workers
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suite completion remains the test critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Linux-only periodic proc snapshots and JSONL diagnostics
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sample per five seconds plus start/end; absent on Windows and macOS
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded synchronous runner-side I/O with no evidenced material latency

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Six fixed suite entrypoints and the selected test count; diagnostics scale linearly with run duration at one sample per five seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to six suite workers; tests within each suite remain serial and share bounded server leases.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm node_modules and Electron artifacts avoid preparation; suite leases retain their existing bounded server reuse. No cache key or invalidation behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for execution path and sampling frequency; low evidence of any material cost from the new sampling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Proc file sizes vary by host, but are bounded kernel snapshots and the sampling frequency is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression; default local/non-Linux execution retains the prior single disk pass, with only bounded diagnostics on Linux.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Coverage setup clears output, invokes the relocated runner, then c8 reporting and protocol-surface checks consume generated files. On Linux CI the broad coverage pass uses tmpfs and the required disk pass explicitly disables coverage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the E2E runner and then c8 report/check commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One covered broad run and fixed reporting subprocesses; the split disk pass does not emit coverage
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Coverage invoked the old runner path and performed the same report/check sequence against disk-backed broad tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All subprocesses are serialized by the coverage command

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write raw V8 coverage and read it for report generation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with covered child processes in the broad pass only
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same broad-suite coverage collection and reporting
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Coverage serialization and report I/O remain required; tmpfs changes temporary test storage, not the checked-in coverage output root

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of covered Agent Host/provider child processes and loaded source files; the added disk lifecycle pass is excluded from coverage collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The covered broad suite retains up to six concurrent suite workers; report generation follows after completion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Coverage output is deliberately removed before each run, so it is cold by design. Runtime preparation follows the runner's existing warm-artifact checks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from coverage environment flags and runner call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Coverage artifact volume depends on loaded source, but the diff does not increase covered process cardinality with the disk pass.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; path relocation preserves coverage behavior, and split mode avoids duplicating raw coverage in the required disk pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Integration tests for the tmpfs wrapper and startup fixture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new storage-wrapper suite runs six synchronous, stubbed bash invocations; the startup fixture invokes the runner four times with fake integration scripts and explicit disk mode.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly six bash subprocesses per test-suite execution, sequentially
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each tiny stub process is on this integration-test suite's critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create small temporary scripts/logs and remove their directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary directory and three stub executables per case
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixed local filesystem setup/cleanup per case

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the runner four times against six fake suite scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four runner starts and six trivial suite-script starts per invocation, matching the prior fixture's structure
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fixture cardinality used the runner and child wrapper at their former paths

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed six wrapper cases and fixed startup-fixture invocations; no user-controlled or repository-size scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Wrapper cases and runner invocations are serial; each runner internally starts up to the fixture's configured one suite worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Temporary roots are always cold and deleted after the suite. The startup fixture explicitly tests warm reuse and forced repair without entering split mode.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from synchronous subprocess calls and fixed test declarations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host process-start latency varies, but cardinality is small and fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the new validation adds only a small fixed test-infrastructure cost and avoids real mounts through stubs.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The GitHub action paginates changed PR files once, flattens current/previous names, and checks exact paths/prefixes before deciding whether already-allocated integration jobs run the E2E suite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Paginate pull-request changed files through the GitHub API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One paginated API operation per action invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same API request and pagination; only path classification entries changed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detection must complete before the affected output is available

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of changed PR files returned by pagination; prefix matching remains linear in files times a small fixed prefix list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single action invocation and one pagination flow; no changed concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or changed; incomplete API results conservatively run tests as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from unchanged boundary and comparison logic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PR file counts vary, but one added prefix has negligible CPU cost and does not add API calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; relocation updates classification without changing network cardinality or test scheduling for semantically relevant harness changes.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and their runner, integration, host-process, storage, coverage, and detection call paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; the main added work is bounded test infrastructure or an explicit narrowed disk-coverage pass offset by moving the broad Linux CI workload to tmpfs.
